q1_issues.issue: The sealed complement of sk_tell_1 encodes the habitual generic "mire-essence with salt-bloom burns slowly" as one specific burn event rather than the distributing Implication rule a bare-kind-subject verbal generic requires (the seal at statement 29 does use the rule form, so the treatment is also internally inconsistent).

(With mire_essence salt_bloom) severs the restriction: inside the seal the content now reads "mire-essence burns slowly" plus "mire-essence carries salt-bloom", widening the claim from the salt-bloom-bearing essence to mire-essence at large.

(PartOf sk_lantern_1 northcove) is emitted at top level although "of the Northcove" is stated only inside the sealed complement, and the seal-projection table says a referent's possessor / Of links stated only inside P stay sealed.

q2_gaps: a PP-restricted bare-kind subject in a generic ("mire-essence with salt-bloom burns slowly") — the instruction set routes an adjectivally-restricted kind subject into a distributing rule with the restriction as a premise conjunct, but gives no form for a PP restriction and no licensed way to attach a surface preposition to a kind symbol

a rate/degree PP on an event ("burning at full rate") — it answers neither where/when/how/whence/whither nor the aboutness question, so nothing in the oblique rules actually selects the preposition-named `(At …)` fallback the parse used
notes: The attitude routing is otherwise right: tell is non-factive with Experiencer holder + Recipient addressee, no predication of P reaches top level, indefinites minted inside the seals (sk_lantern_2, sk_mist_light_1) stay sealed, and only Name atoms, definite typing and compound-kind decomposition project. "a lantern burning at full rate produces…" correctly takes a witness rather than a rule, since the Existential section makes indefinite-plus-verbal-predicate a witness.
